card_surface: Shortcut's compact story card surface is restrained: in board/kanban columns the card typically carries title, story ID (e.g. sc-1234), estimate, owner avatars, labels, and small status glyphs. VCS state on the card face is communicated via small glyphs/badges next to the story metadata — most commonly a branch glyph when a branch is linked and a pull-request glyph that changes colour/form by PR state (open / merged / closed). Branch name itself, PR title, and CI check details do not render on the card face — those live inside the story detail pane. The Pull Request badge colour shift is one of Shortcut's defining card behaviours: when a linked PR transitions (e.g. merged) the card-level PR badge updates colour to reflect that. There is no first-class CI badge on the card face; CI state is read through the PR badge and through the linked story's workflow state (which VCS event handlers may have advanced). The treatment is consistent with developer-PM tools (Linear, Height) — single small glyph(s), optional colour, no inline labels. [uncertain]
detail_panel: The Shortcut story detail pane (full-page story or side pane) renders a structured VCS section that surfaces all branches, commits, and pull requests linked to the story. For each linked PR the pane shows: repository, PR number, PR title (linkable out to GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket), branch name (head -> base), author, current PR state (Draft / Open / Approved / Merged / Closed), review state ('Review required' / 'Changes requested' / 'Approved'), and CI/pipeline status ('In progress' / 'Failed' / 'Successful'). Pull request labels sync from GitHub/GitLab and are visible on hover over the PR row inside the story pane. Branch rows show an 'Open PR' button when a branch is linked but no PR yet exists; commit rows show SHA, message, author, and timestamp. The pane also exposes the Git Helpers icon (between Story ID and the settings ellipsis) which opens a suggested branch name for the developer to copy — a rare 'create-branch-from-the-card-UI' affordance. Overlapping PRs (multiple PRs against the same story) are shown directly in the story detail view for the GitHub integration. The detail pane is the primary surface for VCS truth; the card face is its compressed summary.
state_coupling: Shortcut's state coupling is one of the most-cited reference implementations of VCS-driven workflow automation under the name 'VCS Event Handlers'. Coupling is opt-in and configured per-VCS-integration (Integrations > GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket > Event Handlers section), with each handler binding a VCS event to a target workflow state. Supported events: Branch associated with Story, Branch merged, Commit associated with Story, Pull Request opened, Pull Request approved, Pull Request review requested (not available for GitLab.com), and Pull Request labeled (not available for Bitbucket Cloud). Typical default chain: Branch created -> 'In Development'; PR opened -> 'Ready for Review'; PR merged / branch merged -> 'Completed'. Handlers are explicitly designed to move stories forward only (unstarted -> in-progress -> completed) and never back. Open-work detection prevents premature transitions: if a story has any other open PR or any non-merged non-deleted branch, the 'PR Opened' / 'Branch Merged' handlers are suppressed for the triggering event. Granularity is per-handler / per-branch-name (handlers can be scoped to specific branch names or label names) rather than per-repo. Story states are no longer updated based on PR-label activity after a story is in completed/deployed state.
draft_vs_ready_state: Shortcut treats GitHub Draft PRs (and GitLab WIP PRs) as a distinct state: they are surfaced inside the story detail pane as Draft, but they do not trigger VCS event handlers. The 'PR Opened' handler fires only when the PR transitions from Draft/WIP to Open (Ready for Review) — at that moment the story advances to whichever workflow state the handler targets. Visually, the draft PR row in the pane is labelled Draft; on the card face the PR glyph reflects the underlying status (draft is rendered as the standard open/neutral state, ready/merged uses the colour shift). There is no separate 'Draft' colour token documented on the card-face glyph, so distinguishing draft vs. ready at the card face is subtle — the primary differentiation is in the pane and via the workflow state transition that ready-PRs trigger.
review_state: Review state is surfaced inside the story detail pane, not on the card face. Each linked PR's row in the pane shows the GitHub/GitLab review state as one of 'Review required', 'Changes requested', or 'Approved'. Two VCS event handlers tie review state to workflow: 'Pull Request review requested' (story moves to a configured 'In Review' state — unavailable for GitLab.com) and 'Pull Request approved' (story can advance to a 'Ready to Merge' or equivalent state). Approval counts (e.g. '2/2 approved') and individual reviewer avatars are not rendered as a dedicated card-face badge — they are present in the PR row via sync with the upstream VCS. The Slack integration can push review-requested and approval events into channels, but inside Shortcut the review signal is read through the PR pill and through workflow state changes triggered by handlers. [uncertain]
dod_checklist: Shortcut does not have a first-class 'Definition of Done' field. Teams implement DoD through three patterns: (1) Sub-tasks — the modern first-class breakdown unit (introduced 2024); sub-tasks are mini-stories that can be estimated, assigned, connected to VCS, and moved across workflow states; a parent story's status auto-advances to 'Started' / 'Done' based on sub-task progress, and the parent card shows a sub-task progress count. (2) Checklists (formerly 'Tasks') — lightweight markdown-style to-do items inside the story description; completion percentage is shown on the story card as a small 'N/M' chip; checklist items can be converted to sub-tasks from the three-dot menu. (3) Story templates — pre-populate the description with a standard DoD checklist for a given story type, used by many teams to bake DoD into intake. DoD does not gate state transitions natively — a story can be moved to Done with an incomplete checklist; only sub-task completion influences the parent's auto-transition logic. Card-face treatment: a small checklist progress indicator (e.g. '3/5') appears when checklists are present; sub-task counts appear similarly.
test_linkage: Shortcut has no native test management module. Test linkage is provided entirely through third-party integrations that surface as linked attachments, comments, or auto-created stories rather than a structured Tests tab. Common patterns: Testmo, Qase, TestRail, and Xray can be wired in via Shortcut's API and webhooks to create or update stories on test failures; CI test runs (GitHub Actions, CircleCI, Buildkite) appear inside the linked PR row as part of pipeline status ('In progress' / 'Failed' / 'Successful') rather than as a separate Tests block. There is no native coverage badge or pass/fail count on the card face; CI pass/fail is collapsed into the PR pipeline status in the detail pane. CI status and test-management linkage are therefore separate axes — CI flows through the VCS integration, test management flows through API/webhook integrations. [uncertain]
cicd_status: CI/CD pipeline status is surfaced inside the story detail pane on each linked PR row as one of 'In progress', 'Failed', or 'Successful' — sourced from the GitHub Checks API, GitLab Pipelines, or Bitbucket Pipelines. Individual check names may be visible depending on the upstream provider's payload, but Shortcut does not expose a dedicated per-check UI. There is no first-class CI badge on the card face; failing CI is communicated via the PR row's pipeline pill and by the absence of a workflow state transition (because event handlers wait for the PR to merge, which usually requires checks to pass). Supported CI providers: anything that integrates with GitHub Checks, GitLab CI Pipelines, or Bitbucket Pipelines (Actions, CircleCI, Buildkite, Jenkins via app, etc.). A failing CI check on a linked PR is not auto-promoted to a story-level risk signal — teams rely on PR pipeline status in the pane plus the lack of an automatic state advance. [uncertain]
release_tagging: Shortcut's primary release/version containers are Iterations (sprint-like time-boxed buckets) and Labels (free-form tags that can be used as release tags such as 'release-2026.05' or 'v3.2'). Iterations are the canonical sprint container and aggregate stories and their burn-down; Labels can be applied to stories to mark them as part of a release group, and PR labels can sync into the story via the 'Pull Request labeled' event handler — a pattern teams use to auto-advance stories when a 'released' label is added in GitHub. Shortcut does not have a dedicated Release object with its own lifecycle (unlike Linear Releases or Jira Fix Version). Milestones group epics for higher-level roadmap scope but are not release tags. A story can carry multiple labels (so multiple release tags) and can belong to one Iteration at a time. On the card face, label chips render inline (typically as small coloured pills) when labels are applied; Iteration assignment is usually shown only in the detail pane and in Iteration views, not on every card.
aggregation: Aggregation in Shortcut is partial and workflow-state based, not VCS-state based. Epic cards aggregate child story counts and status via the Epic Progress feature: an epic shows total stories, count by workflow state, completed-vs-remaining points/count, and an ARC chart of remaining work over time on its detail page. The Velocity Bar Chart on iterations rolls up story count or points completed per iteration. Parent stories with sub-tasks show a sub-task progress indicator. However, there is no native 'X of N child stories have merged PRs' or 'all child branches merged' rollup on the epic/feature card face — the branch/PR glyphs on a card describe only that story's own VCS state, not its children's. This gap is consistent with the rest of the developer-PM category (Linear, Jira, Height) — VCS rollup at the epic level is universally absent or limited to manual reports.
environment_deployment_target: Shortcut does not surface environment or deployment target as a first-class field on stories. There is no Deploys object, no Environments property, and no native staging/production badge. Teams implement environment tracking through three workarounds: (1) Labels — apply 'deployed-staging', 'deployed-production' labels, often via PR label sync using the 'Pull Request labeled' event handler to advance stories; (2) Custom workflow states — model environments as workflow states ('In Staging', 'In Production') and rely on event handlers or manual movement; (3) External webhook into Shortcut's API from a CI/CD deploy job to add labels or move state. Visual treatment is therefore label-chip based, with no dedicated environment pill or deployment timeline. Note: Shortcut release-notes mention that 'Story states are no longer updated based on PR label activity after completed/deployed', which implies the labelled-deploy pattern is widely used in practice. [uncertain]
traceability_completeness: Shortcut does not surface a composite traceability indicator. There is no single visual element on the card or in the pane that shows 'this story has code AND tests AND DoD AND deploy'. Each axis is tracked independently: PR state via the card glyph + PR row in the pane; test linkage via third-party integration attachments; DoD via checklists/sub-tasks; deployment via labels or custom states. Workflow state is the implicit composite — with full event handler chains configured, reaching 'Completed' requires PR merged (and usually CI passing), but Shortcut does not block transitions on incomplete checklists or missing test links. The design philosophy is consistent with developer-PM tools: surface each signal in its own slot rather than collapsing them into a single 'trace complete' badge.
design_pattern: Shortcut's design vocabulary on the card face is icon+colour with optional count — close kin to Linear's pattern. The signature behaviour is the PR badge colour change: when a linked pull request state changes (e.g. merged), the card-level badge shifts colour to reflect it. Branch badges and PR badges appear as separate small glyphs; the pattern is consistent across story types (story, bug, chore) since Shortcut has a unified story model with type as a property. The detail pane shifts to a structured PR widget pattern — one row per PR with repository / number / title / branch / state pill / pipeline status / labels-on-hover, similar to Linear's PR row. Two patterns that differentiate Shortcut from peers: (1) Git Helpers — a card-UI affordance to generate a suggested branch name and start the branch without leaving Shortcut, which is rare in the category; (2) VCS Event Handlers — explicit per-event-to-workflow-state binding rules with open-work detection, which is the most-cited reference implementation for PR-driven state automation. Empty state on the card: no glyph rendered when no branch/PR is linked — no placeholder slot. Aligns with Sand's restrained philosophy: small glyphs on the card, structured rows in the pane, state-via-colour, no inline branch names cluttering the card face. [uncertain]
